title: Chapter 143: Three Personas
html:
The address stunned Chen Ge. “Do you mean the old building deep inside a residential complex, with rubbish piled outside?”

This time, it was Wang Hailong and Wenlong who were shocked. “You’ve been there?”

“I was there the night before last.” Even Chen Ge struggled to believe the coincidence.

“Good, then you know the way. We’ll go tonight. Our father is stubborn, so meet us downstairs and we’ll enter together.”

After drafting the plan, the brothers left.

Wang Shenglong’s old home stood beside the Third Sick Hall. Did the monster escape from there? His condition worsened after his admission. Every clue leads back to that hospital.

Chen Ge watched as the pair of brothers walked away.

Wang Haiming carried one monster out of the Third Sick Hall, and Wang Shenglong may harbor another. Both chose Hai Ming Apartments…

He remembered Xiao Du’s account. The two entities inside Wang Haiming had argued, and one claimed it would kill the other if it did not fear capture by the Red Specter.

Was Wang Shenglong’s monster what frightened the entities inside Wang Haiming? If so, is it on Zhang Ya’s level? Could Wang Shenglong be the most terrifying resident in Hai Ming Apartments?

The problem was too complex to dismiss. Skipping lunch, Chen Ge sat on the Haunted House steps and reasoned through it. Wang Haiming’s monster had feared leaving its host because it sensed another presence. It then forced Xiao Du to provide increasingly large sacrifices—sparrows, stray dogs, and finally a person—as though testing that presence’s tolerance.

Unlike the brazen mirror monster in Chen Ge’s Haunted House, the creature at Hai Ming Apartments acted with extreme caution. It was clearly afraid. Even if the entity attached to Wang Shenglong was not a Red Specter, it must be far stronger than an ordinary ghost.

How terrifying is the Third Sick Hall? Two escaped creatures already surpass the mirror monster. How many more remain sealed inside?

Chen Ge rubbed his temples. If a Three-Star Scenario is this dangerous, what awaits me in the Four-Star School of the Afterlife?

Chen Ge stood and called Doctor Gao. If the doctor was busy, he would investigate alone. After two rings, Doctor Gao answered. “Chen Ge? How can I help?”

“Nothing urgent. I wanted to ask about Men Nan. How is he?”

“A day of rest helped physically, but his prognosis is troubling. I’m afraid his condition is worse than I expected.” Doctor Gao’s voice was grave.

“That shouldn’t be possible.” Chen Ge had resolved the source of Men Nan’s distress and completed the black phone’s mission. His condition should have improved.

“After Men Nan woke, I conducted another psychological assessment and made a startling discovery.”

Doctor Gao moved somewhere more private before continuing. “Three personas exist within Men Nan. The first is the developing personality we see every day. The second identifies as his dead mother. I suspect his mind created her as a defense after he witnessed the murder.”

“What about the third?”

“The third emerges only briefly, so we know little beyond his existence. He remains fixed at the age Men Nan was when his mother died. I cannot communicate with him, but whenever he takes control, Men Nan’s psychological insight increases dramatically.”

“Meaning Men Nan’s talent is related to this third persona?”

“Yes. I’ve never encountered anyone more gifted.” Doctor Gao’s admiration was clear. “But preserving that gift complicates treatment. Standard medication would strengthen his primary persona and weaken the others, perhaps destroying his talent. I’m consulting specialists to design a treatment specifically for him.”

Recovery might cost Men Nan his talent; whether that was good or bad, Chen Ge could not decide. Believing Doctor Gao busy, he chose not to mention Wang Shenglong. “All right. I hope Men Nan recovers soon. Goodbye.”

Before he could hang up, Doctor Gao stopped him. “You called for a reason. Men Nan is currently too weak for psychological treatment, so I have time. Tell me what you need.”

Chen Ge described Wang Shenglong’s case. After a thoughtful silence, Doctor Gao said, “I’ll come tonight. Men Nan’s personal belongings are still at Hai Ming Apartments, and I’ve been meaning to retrieve them.”

“Thank you, Doctor Gao.”

“No thanks needed. Ru Xue has told me about you. You’re a psychology enthusiast willing to apply your knowledge to help others. Honestly, your dedication shames me.”

“A psychology enthusiast? That’s how Gao Ru Xue described me?” Chen Ge did not know whether to laugh or cry. There had clearly been a misunderstanding.

“Your Haunted House uses many psychological techniques, so you’ve obviously studied the subject.” Doctor Gao laughed. “I should visit someday.”

“You flatter me.” Chen Ge wiped sweat from his forehead. Half an hour inside the Haunted House might demolish the dignified doctor’s entire image.

Doctor Gao grew serious. “Many people study psychology independently, but few act for the patients’ sake. You helped Wang Xin, and when you called about another case, I was moved. Only those who understand psychological trauma recognize that pain. I’ve wanted to thank you for both Wang Xin and Men Nan. You helped free them from their shackles and breathe again.”

Doctor Gao’s praise left Chen Ge so dazed that he scarcely remembered ending the call. No one had ever spoken of him that way. Perhaps he truly was a noble person.
